panelNumbering: For each 2x2 sheet, panels are numbered left-to-right, top row first: 1, 2, then bottom row: 3, 4.

sheets.title: Act 1 Greyharbour lighting and place test
notes: Use full contact sheets only. Do not crop individual panels; refer to panels by sheet id and panel number.
Act 1 lighting should separate source colors: Lanterna is blue-aluminium bone white, beeswax candles are honey yellow, wood fires are yellow-orange.
Strong Greyharbour target: darkness, route readability, reflections from non-Lanterna sources, scale, and light-source separation work well.
Reflections from fixed non-Lanterna lights may be baked into the art when the reflective surface justifies them.
Left-side navigation/readability is ambiguous at a glance.
Useful for lighting and inhabited clutter, but route direction needs clearer path grammar.
Direction of travel is unclear. At a glance, it is ambiguous whether the bottom-right stairs are traversable.
Interactive-button support is not enough; basic route affordance should read without UI.
Source and effect of light are strong.
The lights in the windows are a good Act 1 Greyharbour reference: fixed beeswax/domestic light should read as inhabited warmth inside the dark structure, not as global ambient fill.
Detail is about 5% too busy for a poor, run-down area; reduce finicky marks while preserving the excellent light logic.

sheets.title: Act 2 Necropolis lighting and stone architecture test
notes: Act 2 Necropolis lighting should use deep desaturated teal-green / blue-green mineral fog light, with Lanterna as pale blue-aluminium bone white.
Stone should dominate; use sweeping circular architectural motifs and avoid wood-dominant structures.
Keep this sheet primarily as a component reference rather than a clean whole-scene target.
Act 2 should feel architectural and ritualized: cold, formal, stone, circular, recursive, symmetrical, and dead. It should not feel ruined-random.
Use round and square geometry. Avoid oval holes, asymmetrical almost-circles, lit unreachable clutter, and non-uniform circular platforms.
Keep the round monumental door concept, concentric threshold language, heavy stone monumentality, and Lanterna color.
Do not keep the asymmetry. Central round doors and circular motifs must be geometrically disciplined and symmetrical.
Best Act 2 green source-color reference on this sheet: deep desaturated teal-green / blue-green, cold and undead rather than neon.
Reject the oval hole in the ground. Necropolis voids, wells, and cuts should be round or square, not oval.
Useful for crypt layout, sarcophagi, and green funerary fixtures.
Less iconic than the other panels; avoid drifting into conventional evenly arranged crypt-room art.
Best light diffusion reference on this sheet: the green lights down in the well are excellent, slightly foggy, and worth reusing.
The circular glass/stone implant on the upper platform is excellent and should become an Act 2 motif.
Reject the small lit platform on the left as clutter: if something is lit, it reads as important or reachable; do not light unreachable distractions.
The lower platform/ring should be uniform if it is meant to be formal circular Necropolis architecture.

sheets.title: Act 3 beyond the Necropolis darkness and colossal ruin test
notes: Act 3 is beyond the walls of the Necropolis: ancient ruins, colossal landscape features, riven trees, dead roads, black ravines, and lethal darkness.
Light should be stricter than Acts 1 and 2: primarily pale blue-aluminium Lanterna light, with only rare campfire or fiery statue attack light.
No settlement candles, domestic warmth, normal Necropolis fixtures, or broad ambient fill.

panels.place: Dead road beneath colossal broken statues

sheets.title: Act 3 Backlands proper open underground landscape test
notes: Backlands proper are open-air underground landscapes inside an immense cavern whose ceiling has never been reached.
Do not conflate underground with tunnels, cave rooms, or dungeon interiors.
No squared-off stone, dressed masonry, formal Necropolis motifs, or carved corridor language.
Lighting should be extremely strict: mostly pale blue-aluminium Lanterna only, with rare campfire/fire as a concrete source.
This sheet is useful, but it is far too bright overall and behaves as if ambient exposure is present across the whole scene.

Distant features are over-visible; mountains and background forms should not be readable from a foreground Lanterna pool unless a concrete distant light source or rare path-finding cue justifies them.
The Backlands should not fill the whole frame with described landscape. Large areas should fall fully into blackness.
Reduce small mark-making in grass, reeds, branches, rocks, roots, and ground texture. The Backlands need to be more empty, darker, and less explained.
The map should show a small playable fragment, a major silhouette or landmark when needed, and then let the rest disappear.
Preferred over panel 3 because it has clearer walkable paths and better game readability.
Too bright overall; distant mountains/background forms are too visible for a foreground Lanterna-lit scene.
Strong landscape feature reference. Major Backlands landmarks of this kind should appear roughly every 4-5 maps.
Still too bright and too descriptive overall.
Too similar in image type to panel 1, but less useful because the walkable path grammar is weaker.
Too bright and too busy with small marks.
Strong mixed-source light reference: good blending of yellow-orange campfire and pale blue-white Lanterna.
Still too bright and too descriptive for Backlands default darkness.

sheets.title: Act 3 Backlands vast landscape darkness test
notes: Generated after the Backlands brightness correction: use giant landscape scale without ambient exposure.
Most of the landscape should fall into blackness; only the Lanterna-lit playable fragment and critical silhouettes should read.
No squared-off stone, no formal Necropolis architecture, and no filled-frame landscape texture.
This sheet is much better on lighting conditions and should be used as the Backlands darkness baseline.
Main remaining problem: too much incidental grit and pointless ground clutter. Odd growths, speckles, grass strokes, rootlets, and busy ground texture reduce the sense of spooky endless space.
For the Backlands, delete incidental ground clutter before deleting darkness. Use fewer, larger marks; keep route shape, one landmark/silhouette, and terrain edges needed for play.
Looks good for darkness, scale, and mood.
Route fails: the path appears to run out at the top, so it does not clearly support traversal. Needs clearer continuation, destination, or threshold.
The silhouetted tree works well. It proves a major Backlands landscape feature can read without explaining the whole space.
Strong bridge/root crossing structure.
Useful map-language: lit near route, dark crossing, partial continuation. The right-hand path near the Lanterna could plausibly connect into the lower approach of panel 1.

panels.place: Tiny campfire at a cliff hollow
notes: Useful as a campfire/refuge reference if it keeps the same dark restraint.
Should not become the default Backlands mood.
